source_refs.note: Exercise 8.2 Q2 (Regula-Falsi, 2 d.p.) on book p. 244; answers p. 307 (printed under '3.')

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the real roots of nonlinear equations correct to 2 decimal places using the Regula-Falsi method, by finding some interval of sign change if not specified. \(3x^3 - 9x^2 + 8 = 0 ; [2, 3]\)
blocks.explanation:
A Regula-Falsi question with the interval \([2, 3]\) given.
Given \(3x^3 - 9x^2 + 8 = 0\); find the root to 2 decimal places.
Plan: secant formula for \(c\), keep the sign-change part, stop at \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).
steps:
Given: \(3x^3 - 9x^2 + 8 = 0\) on the given interval \([2, 3]\).
To find: the root correct to 2 decimal places.
Method: Regula-Falsi. Join \((a, f(a))\) and \((b, f(b))\) by a straight line; where it cuts the x-axis is the next estimate \(c = \frac{a f(b) - b f(a)}{f(b) - f(a)}\). Keep the part where \(f\) still changes sign. Tolerance for 2 decimal places: \(|f(c)| < 0.005\); intermediate values to 4 decimals.

Check continuity and the sign change
\[f(x) = 3x^3 - 9x^2 + 8\]\[f(2) = 24 - 36 + 8 = -4\]\[f(3) = 81 - 81 + 8 = 8\]So \(f(2)\,f(3) < 0\).
Why: \(f\) is continuous everywhere (a polynomial), so by the LRT a root lies in \([2, 3]\).

Iteration 1: \(a = 2,\ b = 3\), \(f(a) = -4,\ f(b) = 8\)
\[c = \dfrac{a f(b) - b f(a)}{f(b) - f(a)}\]\[= \dfrac{(2)(8) - (3)(-4)}{8 - (-4)}\]\[= 2.3333\]\[f(2.3333) = -2.8891 < 0\]
The root lies in \([2.3333, 3]\), so set \(a = c\).
Why: \(f(c)\) has the same sign as \(f(a)\), so the sign change is now between \(c\) and \(b\).

Continue in the same way (table)
The table lists every iteration. Notice that the end \(b\) never moves: the curve bends the same way throughout, so the secant always cuts the axis on the same side of the root.
Why: in Regula-Falsi only the end whose sign matches \(f(c)\) is replaced.

Stop
\[|f(2.6076)| = 0.0045 < 0.005\]So \(c = 2.6076\) is accurate enough; to 2 decimal places \(x \approx 2.61\).
Why: the 8.3.1 tolerance for \(n = 2\) is \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).

Check:
\[f(2.605) = -0.0414\]\[f(2.615) = 0.1019\]Opposite signs, so the exact root lies between 2.605 and 2.615 and rounds to 2.61.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Answer key numbering: the answers printed under "3." (2.61, −1.93, 0.85, 0.36) belong to this Question 2.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the real roots of nonlinear equations correct to 2 decimal places using the Regula-Falsi method, by finding some interval of sign change if not specified. \(x^2 + 4\sin x = 0 ; [-2.2, -1]\)
blocks.explanation:
Regula-Falsi on the given interval \([-2.2, -1]\) (negative numbers: use brackets).
Given \(x^2 + 4\sin x = 0\); find the root to 2 decimal places (radian mode).
Plan: secant formula, keep the sign-change part, stop at \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).
steps:
Given: \(x^2 + 4\sin x = 0\) on the given interval \([-2.2, -1]\).
To find: the root correct to 2 decimal places.
Method: Regula-Falsi. Join \((a, f(a))\) and \((b, f(b))\) by a straight line; where it cuts the x-axis is the next estimate \(c = \frac{a f(b) - b f(a)}{f(b) - f(a)}\). Keep the part where \(f\) still changes sign. Tolerance for 2 decimal places: \(|f(c)| < 0.005\); intermediate values to 4 decimals.

Check continuity and the sign change
\[f(x) = x^2 + 4\sin x\]\[f(-2.2) = 4.84 + 4\sin(-2.2)\]\[= 4.84 - 3.2340 = 1.6060\]\[f(-1) = 1 + 4\sin(-1)\]\[= 1 - 3.3659 = -2.3659\]So \(f(-2.2)\,f(-1) < 0\).
Why: \(f\) is continuous everywhere (a polynomial plus a sine term), so by the LRT a root lies in \([-2.2, -1]\).

Continue in the same way (table)
The table lists every iteration. Notice that the end \(a\) never moves: the curve bends the same way throughout, so the secant always cuts the axis on the same side of the root.
Why: in Regula-Falsi only the end whose sign matches \(f(c)\) is replaced.

Stop
\[|f(-1.9333)| = 0.0024 < 0.005\]So \(c = -1.9333\) is accurate enough; to 2 decimal places \(x \approx -1.93\).
Why: the 8.3.1 tolerance for \(n = 2\) is \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).

Check:
\[f(-1.935) = 0.0066\]\[f(-1.925) = -0.0461\]Opposite signs, so the exact root lies between -1.935 and -1.925 and rounds to -1.93.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) [printed as \(xe_x = 2\)] Find the real roots of nonlinear equations correct to 2 decimal places using the Regula-Falsi method, by finding some interval of sign change if not specified. \(xe^{x} = 2\)
blocks.explanation:
Regula-Falsi with no interval given, so first find one.
Given \(xe^{x} = 2\) (the book prints it as \(xe_x = 2\)); write \(f(x) = xe^{x} - 2\).
Plan: try \(x = 0, 1\) for a sign change, then iterate until \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).
steps:
Given: \(xe^{x} = 2\) (no interval is given, so we first find one).
To find: the root correct to 2 decimal places.
Method: Regula-Falsi. Join \((a, f(a))\) and \((b, f(b))\) by a straight line; where it cuts the x-axis is the next estimate \(c = \frac{a f(b) - b f(a)}{f(b) - f(a)}\). Keep the part where \(f\) still changes sign. Tolerance for 2 decimal places: \(|f(c)| < 0.005\); intermediate values to 4 decimals.

Write the equation as \(f(x) = 0\) and find a sign change
\[f(x) = xe^{x} - 2\]\[f(0) = 0 - 2 = -2\]\[f(1) = e - 2 = 0.7183\]So \(f(0)\,f(1) < 0\).
Why: \(f\) is continuous everywhere (a product of \(x\) and \(e^{x}\)), so by the LRT a root lies in \([0, 1]\).

Continue in the same way (table)
The table lists every iteration. Notice that the end \(b\) never moves: the curve bends the same way throughout, so the secant always cuts the axis on the same side of the root.
Why: in Regula-Falsi only the end whose sign matches \(f(c)\) is replaced.

Stop
\[|f(0.8525)| = 0.0005 < 0.005\]So \(c = 0.8525\) is accurate enough; to 2 decimal places \(x \approx 0.85\).
Why: the 8.3.1 tolerance for \(n = 2\) is \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).

Check:
\[f(0.845) = -0.0329\]\[f(0.855) = 0.0104\]Opposite signs, so the exact root lies between 0.845 and 0.855 and rounds to 0.85.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the equation as \(xe_x = 2\) (with \(x\) as a subscript). It should be \(xe^{x} = 2\); the answer key's 0.85 confirms this.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Find the real roots of nonlinear equations correct to 2 decimal places using the Regula-Falsi method, by finding some interval of sign change if not specified. \(3x + \sin x = e^{x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Regula-Falsi with no interval given.
Given \(3x + \sin x = e^{x}\); write \(f(x) = 3x + \sin x - e^{x}\) and look for sign changes.
Plan: root in \([0, 1]\) first, then the second sign change in \([1, 2]\).
steps:
Given: \(3x + \sin x = e^{x}\) (no interval is given, so we first find one).
To find: the root correct to 2 decimal places.
Method: Regula-Falsi. Join \((a, f(a))\) and \((b, f(b))\) by a straight line; where it cuts the x-axis is the next estimate \(c = \frac{a f(b) - b f(a)}{f(b) - f(a)}\). Keep the part where \(f\) still changes sign. Tolerance for 2 decimal places: \(|f(c)| < 0.005\); intermediate values to 4 decimals.

Write the equation as \(f(x) = 0\) and find a sign change
\[f(x) = 3x + \sin x - e^{x}\]\[f(0) = 0 + 0 - 1 = -1\]\[f(1) = 3 + 0.8415 - 2.7183\]\[= 1.1232\]So \(f(0)\,f(1) < 0\).
Why: \(f\) is continuous everywhere (linear, sine and exponential terms), so by the LRT a root lies in \([0, 1]\).

Iteration 1: \(a = 0,\ b = 1\), \(f(a) = -1,\ f(b) = 1.1232\)
\[c = \dfrac{a f(b) - b f(a)}{f(b) - f(a)}\]\[= \dfrac{(0)(1.1232) - (1)(-1)}{1.1232 - (-1)}\]\[= 0.471\]\[f(0.471) = 0.2652 > 0\]
The root lies in \([0, 0.471]\), so set \(b = c\).
Why: \(f(c)\) has the same sign as \(f(b)\), so the sign change is now between \(a\) and \(c\).

Continue in the same way (table)
The table lists every iteration. Notice that the end \(a\) never moves: the curve bends the same way throughout, so the secant always cuts the axis on the same side of the root.
Why: in Regula-Falsi only the end whose sign matches \(f(c)\) is replaced.

Stop
\[|f(0.3616)| = 0.0029 < 0.005\]So \(c = 0.3616\) is accurate enough; to 2 decimal places \(x \approx 0.36\).
Why: the 8.3.1 tolerance for \(n = 2\) is \(|f(c)| < 0.005\).

Check:
\[f(0.355) = -0.0136\]\[f(0.365) = 0.0114\]Opposite signs, so the exact root lies between 0.355 and 0.365 and rounds to 0.36.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key gives only 0.36. The equation has a second real root: \(f(1) > 0\) and \(f(2) = -0.4798 < 0\). Regula-Falsi on \([1, 2]\) gives 1.7007, 1.8689, 1.8879, 1.8898 with \(|f(1.8898)| = 0.0009 < 0.005\), so the second root is \(x \approx 1.89\).
